headline: SCRIPTED SITCOMS ON INSTAGRAM WENT FROM 44 EPISODES LAST OCTOBER TO 136 THIS OCTOBER, BRANDS ARE PAYING TEN TO A HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS AN EPISODE FOR THEM, AND THE THING THAT MAKES THEM WORK IS THAT NO EPISODE NEEDS YOU TO HAVE SEEN THE LAST ONE
deck: Business Insider published the first real count of this format this morning, and the count is the story.  Episode supply tripled in twelve months.  Brand money is already inside it, at ten thousand to a hundred thousand dollars a show.  And every producer quoted gives the same reason it works, which is the exact opposite of how every brand series you have ever been pitched was sold to you.  These shows are built so that nobody ever needs to have watched the previous one.
tldr: Scripted short-form sitcoms on Instagram went from 44 episodes in October 2025 to 136 in October 2026 on one producer's count, with brand deals running 10,000 to 100,000 dollars, and every producer says the format works because no episode requires you to have seen the previous one.  Take your branded show in development and cut anything whose job is catching the viewer up, then ask any show you are pitched for its share count per episode across its last six episodes rather than its total views.

Chronova Engineering has run the same test on his own channel 43 videos deep: his serialised pocket-watch episodes do 63,000 to 191,000 views and his standalone invention films do 564,000 to 4.6 million, at the same length, on the same bench, with one hobby Stirling-engine shop as his only sponsor across eight uploads.  Split your last twenty uploads into ones that need a previous video and ones that do not, compare the medians, and if you sell cutting tools or measuring instruments offer him three films where your capability is the design constraint.

Seventy-one percent of traditional television political spending ran during sports events this cycle on iSpot's count, up from 56 percent in 2024 and 30 percent in 2022, out of a record 11.87 billion dollar total that put 2.6 billion into connected television.  Re-quote only your pre-empted and deferred sports-adjacent video buys this week, state by state, starting with Maine, Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Kansas, and leave the rest of your schedule alone because the evidence does not support asking there.

Ikea's four-person rapid response team spends nothing on production, uses existing product photography about half the time, and had a post end up inside Apple's silver-winning Cannes Lions entry, while its own named failure was a post that went live in under ten hours and was still too early for the reference.  Set up one lane with a named owner, a fifteen-minute standing slot and no production budget, and add two questions to every reactive brief: has this reference peaked, and does the picture work with the sound off and no caption.

Meta shipped a free macOS editor with a multi-track timeline, 4K watermark-free export, log conversion, custom grade and font import, and Instagram's own cleared audio library, which moves music clearance risk on Reels deliverables from your legal team to Meta's.  Cut one real deliverable in it this week and compare the export against your current tool, send your brand look-up table and fonts to every creator you work with, and write the rule that an in-app track is cleared for Instagram and Facebook and nowhere else.

Facebook extended Creator Fast Track to Brazil paying million-follower creators up to 900 dollars in total for 20 Reels a month over three months, against 3,000 dollars a month in the United States eight months ago, with payment tied to follower count on another platform rather than to any performance measure.  Ask every creator you contract which platform programme they are in and what it obliges them to post, get it in writing, and price your own fees against that much lower reference point.

Teads reported revenue down 26 percent to 235.1 million dollars with a 325.5 million dollar net loss, declined to reinstate guidance, and carries 657 million dollars of debt against 90 million in cash, while AppLovin out-earned the other five listed advertising technology companies combined.  Before committing first-quarter money to any open-web video partner, ask in writing for its connected-television share of revenue and its cash against its debt, and make sure every annual commitment has a termination right you could actually use.
